transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I can’t seem to stay focused long enough to get through all the reports and planning tasks my job requires anymore, especially since taking on a larger service line. My primary care doctor suggested my lifelong focus difficulties might actually be undiagnosed ADHD rather than just stress, which is why I'm seeking this evaluation.
Have you experienced symptoms of restlessness, fidgeting, or an inability to engage in quiet leisure activities, in addition to your difficulties with focus and attention?

No, I don't really experience physical restlessness or fidgeting at all. My struggles are much more about my internal focus, attention, and trying to stay organized rather than physical hyperactivity.

Can you tell me more about your difficulties with organization and if you have trouble following through on instructions, completing tasks, or making careless mistakes in your work or daily activities?

Yes, if someone emails me a list of tasks, I'll usually start the first one but then get distracted and completely forget the rest until they follow up. I'm also constantly misplacing essential items like my badge or meeting notebook, despite trying to use color-coded systems to stay organized. Anything that requires deep, sustained concentration feels so mentally exhausting that I find myself avoiding it by jumping to easier tasks.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others, blurting out answers before questions have been completed, or having difficulty waiting for your turn in conversations or lines?

No, I don't really struggle with those things; I don't typically interrupt people, blurt out answers, or have trouble waiting my turn. My difficulties are much more about losing focus, drifting off during conversations, and struggling to keep up with my tasks.
Can you describe how long you've been experiencing these difficulties with focus, attention, and organization, and whether they've been present since childhood or have developed more recently?

They became significantly worse and highly disruptive about two years ago when I took on my expanded role at work. However, these issues actually trace back to my childhood; in elementary school, teachers always noted I was daydreaming, and my parents had to sit with me for hours just to keep me on track with homework.
Have you ever experienced periods in your life, especially during childhood, where you did exhibit significant restlessness, fidgeting, or hyperactivity, even if those symptoms are not present now?

No, I never really had those physical symptoms as a child either. My struggles back then were much more quiet and internal, like being described as a "daydreamer" who missed instructions. I would just constantly lose track of my homework and need my parents to sit with me for hours to get it done, rather than being physically hyperactive.

Have you ever felt like you were more hyperactive or restless in certain situations, such as during sports, playing with friends, or in other non-structured settings, even if it wasn't noticed in a classroom or at home?

No, I don't recall feeling particularly hyperactive or restless in those situations either. My struggles have always been much more about daydreaming, losing focus, and drifting off rather than physical restlessness. Even in those settings, I was just a quiet kid who got easily distracted.
Can you think of any situations or tasks where you're able to focus and maintain attention without getting distracted, such as hobbies or activities you enjoy?

Honestly, I can't really think of any hobbies or activities where I can focus easily right now. I feel so mentally exhausted from trying to keep up at work that even in my free time, I'm just too distracted and tired to engage in anything that requires attention.

You mentioned that your focus difficulties have been present since childhood, but they became significantly worse about two years ago with your expanded work role. Can you clarify if there were any periods in your life, such as during adolescence or young adulthood, where your focus and attention symptoms improved or were less problematic before worsening again?

I don't recall any specific periods where my symptoms truly went away or improved significantly. I think I was just compensating incredibly hard with strict routines and working extra hours to keep things under control, so it's difficult to point to a time when those focus struggles weren't a factor.

Have you ever received any accommodations or support in academic or professional settings to help manage your focus and attention difficulties, such as extra time to complete assignments or the use of a planner or organizer?

No, I’ve never received any formal accommodations in school or at work. Instead, I always had to rely on my own intense coping mechanisms like meticulous color-coded spreadsheets, over-preparation, and late-night work sessions fueled by coffee. When I was a child, my only support was my parents, who had to sit with me at the kitchen table for hours just to keep me on track with my homework.
Can you describe any strategies or techniques you've developed over the years to help you stay focused and manage your attention, and how effective they've been for you?

For years, I relied on meticulous color-coded spreadsheets, over-preparation, and late-night coffee-fueled work sessions to keep myself afloat. However, those strategies aren't effective in my new role because the sheer volume of projects and rapid task-switching are just too overwhelming. Despite working much longer hours, I'm still falling behind because my old coping mechanisms can't keep up with the demand.
Have you noticed any significant differences in your ability to focus or stay on task when you're working on something that genuinely interests you versus tasks that you find boring or unengaging?

I'm not quite sure, and I haven't really thought about it that way. Honestly, almost all of my work tasks feel so mentally exhausting lately that I struggle to focus on any of them, regardless of what they are. I'm just having a hard time getting through any of it right now.

Do you often find yourself feeling demotivated, disinterested, or disconnected from activities you used to enjoy, or is the issue primarily with sustaining focus and attention on tasks that you need to complete?

It is definitely not a lack of interest or demotivation, as I really want to do my work and know how important it is. The real issue is that forcing myself to concentrate on tasks like long reports or planning is incredibly mentally exhausting. My mind just drifts off after about ten minutes, and I struggle immensely to sustain the focus needed to get them done.
Can you estimate how much of an impact your focus and attention difficulties have on your daily life and work, on a scale from 1 to 10, with 1 being minimal impact and 10 being severe impact?

I would rate the impact around a 7 or 8 out of 10. While I’m barely keeping things afloat by working exhausting, long hours, the constant anxiety of dropping balls and getting irritated feedback from colleagues makes it feel completely unsustainable. It is taking a heavy toll on my professional credibility, which makes the situation feel very severe.

You mentioned that your focus difficulties have been present since childhood but became significantly worse about two years ago with your expanded work role. Can you think of any other significant life changes or stressors around that time that might have contributed to the worsening of your symptoms?

Yes, the main stressors were definitely work-related. When I was promoted to oversee a larger service line, my volume of meetings, strategic reports, and deadlines dramatically increased. At the same time, my health system went through a major EPIC electronic record upgrade and tackled COVID-related backlog initiatives, which completely overwhelmed my coping strategies.

Can you confirm if you have experienced any symptoms of inattention, such as making careless mistakes or difficulty sustaining attention in tasks, in multiple settings, like at work, home, or school, and if these symptoms have been persistent across different situations and environments?

Yes, these issues definitely occur in multiple settings, as I constantly lose essential items like my keys and planner at home just as much as my badge at work. This has been a lifelong pattern going back to elementary school, where teachers noted my daydreaming and my parents had to sit with me for hours at the kitchen table just to keep me on track. While I managed to compensate for these difficulties for years, they have recently become completely overwhelming.

Are you certain you have never exhibited any symptoms of hyperactivity, such as feeling fidgety or restless, even in situations where you were under less stress or pressure, like during vacations or breaks from work?

Yes, I'm quite certain. I don't recall ever feeling particularly hyperactive, fidgety, or restless, even during calmer times like vacations. My struggles have always been much more about focus, getting distracted, and daydreaming.
Are there any situations, such as when you're excited or engaged in a favorite activity, where you might feel more restless or have trouble sitting still, even if it's not a typical behavior for you?

No, even when I'm excited or highly engaged in something, I don't really experience physical restlessness or trouble sitting still. My difficulties are much more about losing focus, daydreaming, or getting mentally exhausted rather than feeling physically hyperactive.

Can you think of any situation in the past or present where you felt overly energetic or restless, even if it was just for a brief period, such as during exercise, playing sports, or engaging in highly stimulating activities?

No, I really can't recall any times where I felt overly energetic or physically restless, even in those situations. My difficulties have always been much more about struggling to focus, daydreaming, and feeling mentally drained rather than having too much energy.
Are you absolutely sure you've never had any periods in your life where you felt excessively energetic or restless, even if it was just for a short time or in a specific context?

Yes, I'm absolutely sure. I don't recall ever having periods where I felt excessively energetic or restless, even for a short time. My struggles have always been about my mind drifting off and losing focus, rather than having too much energy.
Can you describe any differences in how your focus and attention difficulties manifest when you are under pressure to meet a deadline versus when you have more flexible or open-ended tasks?

I haven't really thought about it in those exact terms, so I'm not sure of a clear difference. However, I do know that open-ended tasks with no immediate pressure are the ones where I find myself procrastinating the most. I constantly make excuses to avoid starting them because they just feel so overwhelming to initiate.
Have you noticed any difficulties with following detailed instructions or making mistakes due to not fully attending to details in your work or daily activities?

Yes, I definitely struggle with following through on detailed instructions. For instance, if I get an email with multiple tasks—like approving a budget change, scheduling a follow-up, and writing a summary—I’ll do the first task but then get distracted and completely forget the rest. These missed details have unfortunately led to delayed reports and dropped follow-ups that hurt my credibility.
Can you describe how you feel when you're able to successfully complete a task without getting distracted, and does that ever give you a sense of motivation or energy to tackle more tasks?

To be honest, it's been so long since I've been able to complete a complex task smoothly without getting distracted that I'm not really sure. When I do manage to finish something these days, I usually just feel incredibly exhausted and relieved rather than energized or motivated.

Can you confirm if your difficulties with focus, attention, and organization have been consistently present across most areas of your life, including work, home, and social situations, or are they more situation-specific?

Yes, they are definitely present across multiple areas of my life, including at home where I constantly misplace my keys or notebooks and rely on strict routines just to get by. This isn't a new development either, as this pattern goes all the way back to my childhood, affecting both my schoolwork and my daily life at home from a very young age.

Can you describe any instances where you felt like you were able to focus and complete tasks with ease, perhaps during periods of high interest or low stress, and how those experiences compare to your current challenges?

To be honest, I can't really recall any times in my life when focusing and completing tasks felt truly easy, even when I was highly interested in them. I have always had to rely on intense compensation strategies and sheer extra effort just to get things done. It has never felt effortless; I've just always had to work much harder behind the scenes to make it happen.
Can you estimate how often you find yourself getting distracted by unrelated thoughts or stimuli when you're trying to focus on a task, and does this happen almost daily?

Yes, this absolutely happens on an almost daily basis, especially when I'm trying to focus on demanding tasks like reports or long meetings. After about ten minutes, my mind will start to drift and I'll realize I've been staring at the same EPIC dashboard without absorbing anything, or I'll find myself constantly getting distracted by easier tasks like checking email or getting coffee.

Can you tell me more about how your difficulties with focus and attention affect your ability to learn new information or skills, and do you find that you need to repeat information to yourself or use additional strategies to remember it?

Yes, absorbing new information is incredibly difficult because my mind constantly drifts during meetings or while reading reports, forcing me to reread things multiple times or ask people to repeat themselves. To cope and actually remember things, I've always relied on heavy over-preparation, meticulous color-coded spreadsheets, and late-night work sessions. However, with my expanded workload now, those exhausting strategies are simply no longer enough to keep me from falling behind.

You mentioned that your focus difficulties have been present since childhood but significantly worsened about two years ago. Can you clarify if you believe the recent increase in workload and stressors, such as the EPIC electronic record upgrade and COVID-related initiatives, triggered the worsening of your symptoms, or do you think it's more related to the inherent demands of your new role?

Honestly, it feels like a combination of both. The inherent demands of my new role—such as juggling multiple projects, writing strategic reports, and constantly switching between dashboards and budget models—were already a major stretch. However, the added pressure of the EPIC upgrade and COVID backlog initiatives happening at the same time completely overwhelmed my coping strategies and triggered the noticeable worsening.

Can you think of any situations where you're able to maintain focus and attention without getting distracted for an extended period, and if so, what factors contribute to your ability to focus in those situations?

Honestly, I struggle to think of any situations lately where I can maintain my focus for an extended period. In the past, I used to rely on late-night, coffee-fueled sessions with high pressure to force myself to concentrate, but lately, even those coping mechanisms aren't working. I just feel constantly distracted and mentally exhausted now.
Can you describe any significant changes in your focus and attention difficulties over time, particularly in relation to changes in your life circumstances, stress levels, or other factors?

My focus difficulties actually start back in childhood, when teachers noted my daydreaming on report cards, but I managed to compensate for years with intense routines. However, things became significantly worse about two and a half years ago when I was promoted to oversee a larger service line. The sudden increase in meetings and reports, combined with our electronic record upgrade and COVID backlog initiatives, completely overwhelmed my lifelong coping strategies.
